standard_prerequisites: Chapter lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated (source lemma, worklist row 72): a finitely generated algebraic extension is finite; here k(alpha, beta)/k is generated by the two algebraic elements alpha, beta
Chapter lemma-finite-is-algebraic (delivered card L48360): a finite extension is algebraic; subextensions of finite extensions are finite
core_obligations: For alpha, beta algebraic over k, the extension k(alpha, beta)/k is finite by the finitely-generated lemma
k(alpha + beta) is a subextension of the finite extension k(alpha, beta)/k, hence finite over k, hence alpha + beta is algebraic over k by the finite-is-algebraic lemma
The same subextension argument applies verbatim to the difference, product and quotient, all of which lie in k(alpha, beta)
proof_roadmap: Build the finite extension generated by the two elements
Read off algebraicity of each rational expression from the finite subextension
